mainTopic: When a קטנה's מיאון cancels a גט, and who may marry her afterwards
overview: The משנה teaches that when a young girl (קטנה) leaves a man, what counts is how she left him. If she left him with a גט, she may not go back to him. If she left him by מיאון, she may. The גמרא finds two parts of the משנה that seem to clash over whether a מיאון cancels an earlier גט. שמואל says the two parts come from different תנאים. רבא instead explains that a girl's מיאון against the same man is different from a מיאון against another man. רבא then shows a real clash between two cases about another man. רבי אלעזר answers that the משנה has two authors, and עולא answers that the strict case is a girl divorced three times, who looks like an adult. A story about questions sent to רבי עקיבא in prison names the strict תנאים. רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי tells the story differently, as a question about מיאון after a death for the sake of יבום. Two versions of רב יצחק בר אשיאן disagree about whether she may marry the ex-husband's brother. A new משנה about a remarried divorcee and the יבם then begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The basic rule: which came last, the divorce or the refusal?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states a general rule. If a גט came after a מיאון, she may not go back to that man. If a מיאון came after a גט, she may go back.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: if the divorce came after the refusal, she may not go back to him. If the refusal came after the divorce, she may go back to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a short rule about a young girl (קטנה) who was married and left her husband. What matters is how her last exit from that man happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטנה can leave a marriage in two ways: מיאון (refusal, which shows the marriage was never fully binding) or a גט (a regular divorce). If her final exit was a מיאון, it is clear she was a קטנה, so she may go back to him. If her final exit was a גט, she looks like a normal divorcée, so she may not go back to him once she has remarried.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
A bill of divorce
Refusal: a קטנה married by her mother or brothers declares she does not want the marriage
She is forbidden to go back to him
Permitted

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two orders. 'גט after מיאון' means the גט was LAST, so she is forbidden. 'מיאון after גט' means the מיאון was LAST, so she is permitted. The one that came last decides.

phrases.english: This is the principle:
If the bill of divorce came after the refusal,
she is forbidden to return to him;
if the refusal came after the bill of divorce,
she is permitted to return to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section with the summary rule of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The last way she left a man decides: a גט at the end forbids her to return to him, and a מיאון at the end permits it.

steps.title: A girl married to four men in a row
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes a girl who refused one man, was divorced by a second, refused a third, and was divorced by a fourth. Anyone she left with a גט is forbidden to her. Anyone she left with מיאון is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: A girl refuses one man, then marries another who divorces her, then marries another and refuses him, then marries another who divorces her. The rule is: anyone she leaves with a divorce, she may not go back to. Anyone she leaves by refusal, she may go back to.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a longer case with four husbands and applies the rule to each of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here each husband is judged by how she left him. The first and third husbands she left by מיאון, so she may go back to them. The second and fourth gave her a גט, so she may not go back to them, even though she married someone else afterwards.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl who does מיאון (refuses)
And she married another man
And he divorced her
That she leaves from him

steps.whatToRemember: Husband by husband: a גט means she may not go back to him, and מיאון means she may.

phrases.english: A girl who refuses a man
and marries another, and he divorces her,
then marries another, and she refuses him,
phrases.notes: The משנה leaves out 'she marries', but it means she married a third man.

phrases.english: then another, and he divorces her,
this is the principle:
anyone she leaves by means of a bill of divorce,
she is forbidden to return to him;
anyone she leaves by means of refusal,
she is permitted to return to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the general rule to a longer chain of marriages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each husband is judged by how she left him: a גט forbids going back to him, and מיאון permits it.

steps.title: The גמרא's reading: a refusal cancels a divorce
steps.stepSummary: From the first rule ('מיאון after גט, she is permitted'), the גמרא concludes that a מיאון can cancel an earlier גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It seems that a refusal comes and cancels a divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by drawing a conclusion from the first rule of the משנה. This sets up the contradiction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first rule, a man gave her a גט, later married her again, and then she did מיאון against him. Since she may go back to him, the earlier גט seems to have lost its power. So the conclusion is that a מיאון wipes out the effect of a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion on the משנה
Apparently, from here we see
Comes
And cancels

phrases.english: Gemara:
Apparently, a refusal comes
phrases.notes: This comes from the first rule: 'refusal after divorce, she is permitted to return to him.'

phrases.english: and cancels a bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general principle out of the first rule of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the first rule we learn that a מיאון cancels a גט.

steps.title: The second case seems to say the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the four-husband case again. Since she may not go back to the man who divorced her, even after a later מיאון against someone else, it seems that a מיאון does NOT cancel a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they point out a contradiction: A girl refuses one man, then marries another who divorces her, then another whom she refuses, then another who divorces her. The rule is: anyone she left with a divorce, she may not go back to. Anyone she left by refusal, she may go back to. So it seems that a refusal against a different man does not come and cancel this man's own divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the second case of the משנה word for word to challenge the conclusion of the previous step. The two parts of the משנה seem to disagree about whether a מיאון cancels a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the four-husband case, the second husband gave her a גט, and after that she did מיאון against the third husband. Yet she still may not go back to the second husband, so the later מיאון did not cancel his גט. The גמרא notices that here the מיאון was against a different man (חבריה), while the גט belongs to this man (דידיה).

keyTerms.meaning: And they point out a contradiction between sources
Of his fellow, meaning a different man
His own גט

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is quoting the same משנה again, not a new source. It repeats the words to set its two parts against each other.
steps.whyThisMatters: This contradiction drives the rest of the discussion. The difference between a מיאון against the same man and a מיאון against a different man is the point the גמרא will now need to sort out.

phrases.english: And they raise a contradiction:
A girl who refuses a man
and marries another, and he divorces her,
then another, and she refuses him,
then another, and he divorces her,
this is the principle:
anyone she left by means of a bill of divorce,
she is forbidden to return to him;
anyone she left by refusal, she is permitted to return to him.
Apparently, the refusal of another man does not come
phrases.notes: Think of the second husband: he gave a גט, and her later refusal of the third husband doesn't free her to go back to him.

phrases.english: and cancel his own bill of divorce.
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording, so read it as 'וּמְבַטֵּיל', 'and cancels'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 3's conclusion by using the second half of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that a מיאון cancels a גט (step 3).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the four-husband case, a later מיאון does not free her to go back to the husband who gave a גט. That suggests a מיאון does not cancel a גט, which goes against the first rule.

steps.title: שמואל: Two different authors wrote these two rulings
steps.stepSummary: שמואל resolves the contradiction by saying the two parts of the משנה come from two different תנאים who disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: This משנה is broken. Whoever taught this ruling did not teach that ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the contradiction from Step 4. He says the two rulings were taught by different people who hold different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ruling holds that a מיאון cancels a גט. The four-husband case holds that it does not. שמואל does not try to reconcile them. He says each ruling reflects a different תנא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'break it'. It means the משנה is split and its parts do not come from one author.

keyTerms.term: מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: The one who taught this did not teach that. The two rulings come from different authors.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
It is broken (disjointed);
phrases.notes: He means the משנה is not one smooth piece. Its two halves come from two different teachers.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ.
phrases.english: whoever taught this did not teach that.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּבְרַהּ, מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings come from one author, so they must agree.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rulings come from two authors who disagree about whether a מיאון cancels a גט.

steps.title: רבא: There is no contradiction. Her refusal of the same man is different
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the contradiction. A מיאון against the same man cancels that man's own גט. A מיאון against a different man does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the difficulty? Perhaps her מיאון against him cancels his own גט, while her מיאון against another man does not cancel his גט.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא says שמואל's answer is not needed, because the two rulings do not really contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ruling is about a woman who refused the same man who had divorced her. The four-husband case is about refusing a different man. רבא suggests the law treats these two situations differently, so both rulings can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difficulty? A way of saying there is no real problem.
But perhaps.
His own.
Of his fellow, meaning a different man.

phrases.english: Rava said: And what is the difficulty?

phrases.aramaic: וְדִלְמָא: מֵיאוּן דִּידֵיהּ מְבַטֵּל גֵּט דִּידֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Perhaps refusal of him cancels his own bill of divorce,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the man who divorced her. She later remarried him and then refused him.

phrases.aramaic: מֵיאוּן דְּחַבְרֵיהּ לָא מְבַטֵּל גִּיטָּא דִידֵיהּ.
phrases.english: while refusal of the other man does not cancel his bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from שמואל by denying that the contradiction exists.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the contradiction from Step 4, so שמואל's answer becomes unnecessary.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The contradiction treated a מיאון against the same man and a מיאון against a different man as the same thing.

steps.title: Challenge: The same worry should apply to both cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a מיאון against another man fails to cancel the גט. The reason seems to be that the first husband might lure her back. That same reason should stop her own מיאון against him from cancelling his גט too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is a מיאון against another man different, so that it does not cancel the first man's גט? It is because she knows the first husband's hints and winks, so he will go and lead her astray and bring her back to himself. If so, her מיאון against him also should not cancel his own גט, since she knows his hints and winks and he will go and lead her astray and bring her back!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רבא's distinction. It argues that the reason behind his rule should apply to both cases equally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given is a concern that the first husband will use his familiar signals to pull her away from her new husband. That same concern exists whenever she was once his wife. So it should block her return in both cases, and רבא's distinction seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? It asks for the reason behind a distinction.
Since, because.
His hints and winks, meaning his private signals that she knows well.
Leads astray, disrupts.

phrases.english: And what is different about refusal of the other man
that it does not cancel his bill of divorce?
Since she recognizes his hints and winks,
he will go, lead her astray, and bring her back to himself.
phrases.notes: The fear is that he gets her to refuse her new husband so she can come back to him.

phrases.aramaic: מֵיאוּן דִידֵיהּ נָמֵי לָא לִיבַטֵּל גִּיטָּא דִידֵיהּ —
phrases.english: Then her refusal of him should also not cancel his bill of divorce,
since she recognizes his hints and winks,
he will go, lead her astray, and bring her back!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מֵיאוּן דְּחַבְרֵיהּ דְּלָא מְבַטֵּל גִּיטָּא דִידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's distinction from Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's distinction between her מיאון against the same man and her מיאון against a different man.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason for the rule is the fear that he will lure her back. That fear applies in both cases, so the law should be the same in both.

steps.title: Answer: He already tried to sway her and failed
steps.stepSummary: When she refused the same man, he had already remarried her and she still left him. That proves he cannot sway her, so the fear does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he already tried to lead her astray, and she was not led astray.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. The case of refusing the same man is different, because his influence has already been tested and failed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the same-man case, he divorced her, remarried her, and she still refused him. That shows his hints and winks do not work on her. So there is no fear of him luring her back, and his גט can be cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: He already tried to lead her astray.
And she was not led astray.

phrases.english: But he already tried to lead her astray,
phrases.notes: He remarried her after the divorce, and she refused him anyway.

phrases.english: and she was not led astray.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 7 and saves רבא's distinction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction: the fear has already been shown not to apply.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fear of his influence applies equally in both cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: When she refused the same man, she already proved he cannot sway her, so the fear does not apply.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule holds. Her מיאון against the same man cancels his גט, because she already proved he cannot sway her. Her מיאון against a different man does not cancel the first man's גט, because the fear of being lured back still applies.

steps.title: רבא: The real contradiction is between two other-man cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the real difficulty is between two rulings that both involve a מיאון against a different man. Another case in the משנה implies that refusing a different man WOULD let her go back to the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if there is a difficulty, it is the other-man case against the other-man case. The משנה says: If she refused him and he took her back, then gave her a גט, and she married another man and was widowed or divorced, she may not return to him. The reason is that she was widowed or divorced. But if she had refused the other man, she could return to the first. This shows that a מיאון against another man does come and cancel the first man's גט.
steps.whatsHappening: Having defended his distinction, רבא now points out where the real contradiction lies. This sets up the next move in the סוגיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four-husband case says a מיאון against another man does NOT cancel the first man's גט. This new line of the משנה stresses that she was widowed or divorced, which implies a מיאון against the other man WOULD allow her back. Now both sides of the contradiction are about a different man, so רבא's same-man distinction cannot solve it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, if there is a difficulty, it is this. It points to the true problem.
She was widowed.
The reason is. It signals an inference from the exact wording.
But this, meaning the opposite case.
Evidently, it follows that.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two 'other man' cases. In the four-husband case she refused a different man and still may not return to the man who divorced her. In this case, the wording implies that refusing a different man WOULD let her return. That clash is the contradiction.
steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the contradiction to a place רבא's distinction cannot reach. The סוגיא now needs a new answer.

phrases.english: Rather, if there is a difficulty,
it is the other-man case against the other-man case that is difficult:
phrases.notes: Both rulings he is about to compare involve refusing a different man, not the one who gave the גט.

phrases.english: If she refused him and he took her back,
then he gave her a bill of divorce and she married another man,
and she was widowed or divorced,
she is forbidden to return to him.
The reason is that she was widowed or divorced.
But if she had refused the other man, she would be permitted to return to him,
so evidently refusal of the other man comes
and cancels his bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי קַשְׁיָא, דְּחַבְרֵיהּ אַדְּחַבְרֵיהּ קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending his distinction, רבא moves the contradiction to two cases that his distinction cannot separate.
steps.kashyaTarget: The four-husband ruling, where a מיאון against another man does not let her return to the man who divorced her.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording ('widowed or divorced') implies that a מיאון against another man would allow her back. That directly clashes with the four-husband case.

steps.title: The משנה's closing rule says a later refusal does not undo the earlier divorce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a rule that a girl who left any man with a גט may never return to him, even after a later מיאון. So a מיאון against a different man does not cancel the first man's גט. This clashes with the case from step 9.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here is a source that contradicts it: A girl refuses one man, then marries another who divorces her, then marries another and refuses him. The rule is: any man she left with a גט, she may not go back to. Any man she left by refusal, she may go back to. So her refusal of the other man does not cancel the first man's גט!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second half of the contradiction רבא raised in step 9. This source says refusing a different man does NOT let her go back to the man who divorced her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, one case implied that a מיאון against a later husband lets her return to the man who gave her a גט. This rule says the opposite: anyone she left with a גט stays forbidden to her. Both cases involve a מיאון against a different man, so they really do clash.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction (a source that seems to say the opposite)
This is the general rule
Apparently / we see from here
Of his fellow (of the other man)

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
A girl who refuses a man
and married another, and he divorced her,
then married another and refused him,
this is the rule:
anyone she left with a bill of divorce
she is forbidden to return to him;
anyone she left by refusal, she is permitted to return to him.
So we see: a refusal of the other man does not come
and cancel his own divorce!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the contradicting source that רבא pointed to in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The case from step 9 implying that a מיאון against a different man lets her return to the man who divorced her
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sources deal with a מיאון against a different man, yet one lets her go back to the man who divorced her and the other forbids it

steps.title: רבי אלעזר says the משנה comes from two different authors
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that the משנה is split. The two rulings come from two different תנאים who disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Break it apart. Whoever taught this ruling did not teach that one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the contradiction by saying the two rulings come from different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of finding a difference between the cases, רבי אלעזר says the contradiction is real. One תנא holds that a מיאון against another man undoes the earlier גט, and the other תנא holds it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Break it (the משנה is split, not one author)

keyTerms.term: מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: Whoever taught this did not teach that

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: Break it,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה does not hold together as one opinion. Split it into two.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ.
phrases.english: whoever taught this did not teach that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings come from one author, so they must agree
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ruling belongs to a different תנא, so there is no contradiction within one opinion

steps.title: עולא says the strict case is one where she was divorced three times
steps.stepSummary: עולא keeps the משנה as one opinion. In the strict case she was divorced three times, so she looks like an adult. Her later refusal therefore does not undo the divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The strict case is where she was divorced three times, so she looks like an adult.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a different answer. He says the two cases are not the same situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא says the ruling that forbids her to go back deals with a girl who already had three divorces. A girl with that much marriage history looks like a גדולה, so חז"ל did not let her מיאון cancel the גט. In a normal case her מיאון can cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: She was divorced three times
She appears / looks like
An adult woman (who cannot do מיאון)

phrases.english: Ulla said:
for example, where she was divorced three times,
so she looks like an adult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the step 10 contradiction, different from רבי אלעזר's
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two rulings deal with the same kind of girl
steps.terutzMaskana: The strict ruling deals with a girl divorced three times, who looks like an adult

steps.title: Which תנא holds the strict view?
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי אלעזר's split, the גמרא asks who the תנא is that holds the strict view: a later refusal does not let her return to the man who divorced her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who taught this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the strict ruling. This sets up the story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רבי אלעזר says the משנה has two authors, it makes sense to ask who they are. The answer comes through a story about a question asked during a time of danger.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (which sage taught this)?

phrases.english: Who is the Tanna who taught this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי אלעזר's answer by asking who the authors are
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who rules that a later מיאון does not undo an earlier גט

steps.title: רב reads a פסוק about paying for water, and introduces the question asked in a time of danger
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, in the name of רב, quotes the פסוק about buying water with money. He explains that in a time of danger people asked: a girl left her first husband with a גט and her second by מיאון. May she go back to the first?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that רב said: What does the פסוק mean, 'We drank our water for money, our wood comes for a price'? At a time of danger this הלכה was asked: If she left the first husband with a גט and the second by refusal, may she return to the first?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by telling a story. Here it sets up the question that was asked. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question asked is exactly our case: a גט from the first husband, then a מיאון against a different man. The פסוק about paying for water hints that, at that time, getting Torah answers cost money.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written?
A time of danger (persecution)
Was asked / was sought

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"We have drunk our water for money;
phrases.notes: איכה 5:4

this halacha was asked:
If she left the first husband with a bill of divorce
and the second by refusal,

steps.title: רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה בן בתירה both forbid her
steps.stepSummary: People paid a messenger four hundred זוז to ask רבי עקיבא in prison and רבי יהודה בן בתירה in נציבין. Both said she may not go back to the first husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: They hired a man for four hundred זוז, and he asked רבי עקיבא in prison, and he forbade it. They asked רבי יהודה בן בתירה in נציבין, and he forbade it.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the answer: two great sages forbid her to go back. So they are the תנאים who hold the strict view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying four hundred זוז for an answer is the 'water for money' of the פסוק. Both רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה בן בתירה say a later מיאון does not undo the first husband's גט. That matches the strict side of the split משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A silver coin
Prison
Netzivin, a city where רבי יהודה בן בתירה lived
He forbade it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה בן בתירה hold that once a girl left a man with a גט, a later מיאון against someone else does not let her go back to him. They are the תנאים behind the strict ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: This names real authorities for one side of רבי אלעזר's split, so the contradiction is shown to be a true disagreement between תנאים.

phrases.english: They hired one man
phrases.notes: This is the 'water for money' from the פסוק: they had to pay to get a Torah answer.

phrases.english: for four hundred zuz,
and they asked Rabbi Akiva

phrases.aramaic: אֶת רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה בִּנְצִיבִין,
phrases.english: They also asked Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira in Netzivin,
and he forbade it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׂכְרוּ אָדָם אֶחָד בְּאַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת זוּז

steps.title: The question about returning to the first husband was never asked
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי says nobody needed to ask whether she may return to her first husband. If מיאון can remove a כרת prohibition, it can surely remove a plain לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי said: That question was never needed. If her refusal can permit something that carries כרת, it can surely permit something that is only a regular prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי rejects the version of the story in steps 14-15 about what was asked in the time of danger. He says the answer to that question is so obvious that nobody would have asked it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מיאון cancels the second marriage, so she was never a married woman to him. That removes an איסור of כרת, the prohibition of a married woman. If so, the smaller איסור לאו against returning to a former husband after another marriage must surely fall away too. On his view, she may go back to the first husband.

keyTerms.meaning: we did not need it; the question was unnecessary
a prohibition punished by כרת (being cut off)
a prohibition that is a plain negative commandment
all the more so

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei said:
For this we had no need.
phrases.notes: He means the question from steps 14-15, whether she may go back to her first husband, was too obvious to ask.

phrases.english: You permitted a prohibition of כרת,
phrases.notes: Her refusal cancels the second marriage, so living with him was never the sin of a married woman.

phrases.english: so for a prohibition of a plain לאו, is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the version of the question reported in steps 14-15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the question sent to רבי עקיבא was about returning to the first husband.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A קל וחומר makes the answer obvious, so that question would never have been sent.

steps.title: The real question: may she refuse after a death so that יבום can happen
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, the question was about a girl first married to a man's maternal uncle, a rabbinic relative. She later married his paternal brother, who died. May she now refuse the first marriage so that יבום can take place?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what they asked. A girl had been married to a man's mother's brother, so she is a rabbinic relative to him. Then that man's paternal brother married her and died. May she refuse now and cancel the first marriage, so that יבום can happen? In short: does מיאון work after a death, when it would allow the מצוה of יבום?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי gives his own version of the question that was sent to the גדולים. It is a יבום case, not a case of returning to a former husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of the uncle's marriage, she is a שניה, a relative forbidden by rabbinic law, to the surviving brother. That blocks יבום. If her מיאון could cancel the uncle's marriage now, the block would disappear. The real issue is whether מיאון works after the husband has died, when a מצוה is at stake.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, however
the wife of his mother's brother
a secondary relative, forbidden by rabbinic law
her rival wife (another wife of the same husband)
refusal after the husband's death
where a מצוה (here, יבום) is at stake

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two husbands. She refuses the first marriage, to the uncle, not the marriage to the brother who died. Canceling the uncle's marriage is what would make יבום possible.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what they asked:
Suppose she was the wife of his mother's brother,
who is a secondary relative to him,
phrases.notes: A שניה is forbidden by the חכמים, not by the תורה itself.

phrases.english: and his paternal brother married her and died.
What is the law? May she refuse now
and uproot the first marriage,
and (her rival wife) go through יבום?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word 'her rival wife' and some don't. Without it, the question is whether she herself may go through יבום.

phrases.english: Is there refusal after death
where there is a מצוה, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רב's version, רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי supplies the question that was actually asked.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does מיאון work after the husband's death, when it would make יבום possible?

steps.title: רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה בן בתירה forbade it
steps.stepSummary: This time two people were hired for four hundred זוז, and they asked רבי עקיבא in prison and רבי יהודה בן בתירה in נציבין. Both forbade. In this version, they ruled that מיאון does not work after death, even for a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They hired two people for four hundred זוז. The messengers asked רבי עקיבא in prison, and he forbade it. They asked רבי יהודה בן בתירה in נציבין, and he forbade it too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the story of the messengers, now attached to רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's version of the question. Both rabbis said no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story is the same, but what is being forbidden has changed. In this version, the ruling is that she cannot refuse after the death to make יבום possible. It is not a ruling against returning to a first husband.

keyTerms.meaning: they hired
prison
and he forbade it
נציבין, the city where רבי יהודה בן בתירה lived

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of what רבי עקיבא forbade. In רב's version, a girl who refused her second husband may not return to the first, who divorced her. In רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's version, she may return, and what was forbidden was refusing after a death in order to allow יבום.

phrases.aramaic: שָׂכְרוּ שְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם בְּאַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת זוּז,
phrases.english: They hired two people for four hundred זוז,
and they came and asked Rabbi Akiva
in prison, and he forbade it.

phrases.aramaic: אֶת רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה בִּנְצִיבִין, וְאָסַר.
phrases.english: [They asked] Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira in Netzivin, and he forbade it.
phrases.notes: This is the same story as step 15, but here it answers the new יבום question.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׂכְרוּ שְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם בְּאַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת זוּז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer to the question posed in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Forbidden: מיאון after death does not work, even to allow the מצוה of יבום.

steps.title: רב agrees she may marry the brother of the man she is forbidden to
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אשיאן says that רב forbids her to the man who divorced her. Still, רב agrees she is permitted to that man's brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר אשיאן said: Even רב agrees that she may marry the brother of the man to whom she became forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק בר אשיאן limits רב's strict ruling. The ban covers only the man who divorced her, not his brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a man may not marry his brother's divorcée. Here, though, her later מיאון works for the brother, even though it does not undo the divorce for the husband himself. So רב's strictness has a narrow reach.

keyTerms.meaning: and he agrees, concedes
she is permitted
she became forbidden

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even on רב's strict view, the result of the divorce is limited to the husband himself and does not reach his brother.

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Ashyan said:
And Rav agrees,
phrases.notes: This refers back to רב's strict view, that she may not return to the man who divorced her.

phrases.english: that she is permitted to the brother of this man
to whom she became forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַשְׁיָאן: וּמוֹדֶה רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב's strict view from step 14 and sets a limit on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even on רב's view, a girl forbidden to the man who divorced her is permitted to that man's brother.

steps.title: Why say the brother is permitted? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב יצחק בר אשיאן needed to say she is permitted to the brother. The reason for the ban was that she knows her ex-husband's signals, and she does not know the brother's.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious! It is the ex-husband whose hints and winks she recognizes, not his brother's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the statement in step 19, which said she is permitted to the brother. Why would anyone think otherwise?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on the ex-husband is based on a worry: she knows his private signals, so he may have quietly pushed her toward her later refusal. That worry simply does not exist with the brother, whose signals she does not know. So saying the brother is permitted seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. The גמרא asks why a statement was needed at all.
Hints, subtle signals.
Winks, gestures with the eyes.
She recognizes, she is familiar with.

phrases.english: It is obvious!
It is he whom she recognizes
phrases.notes: "He" is the man who divorced her, from step 19.

phrases.english: by his hints and his winks
but his brother, not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב יצחק בר אשיאן's statement in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The clause "she is permitted to his brother"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason for the ban (knowing his signals) clearly does not apply to the brother, so stating the permission seems unnecessary.

steps.title: We might have made a decree banning the brother too
steps.stepSummary: The statement was needed because we might have thought the רבנן would ban the brother as a fence around the ex-husband. He teaches that there is no such decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: let us decree against this one, the brother, because of that one, the ex-husband. So he teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 20. The permission for the brother was worth saying, because one could have imagined a protective decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the real worry does not apply to the brother, the רבנן sometimes ban a safe case so people do not confuse it with a forbidden one. Here someone might fear that seeing her marry the brother would make people think she may marry the ex-husband too. רב יצחק בר אשיאן teaches that, even on רב's view, no such decree was made.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. Introduces the mistaken thought the statement comes to block.
Let us make a decree, a rabbinic protective ban.
Because of, as a fence around something else.
So he teaches us. The statement is needed after all.

phrases.english: You might have said:
Let us decree against this one because of that one
phrases.notes: The first "this one" is the brother. "That one" is the ex-husband.

phrases.english: so he teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Justifies the statement by naming a reasonable mistaken assumption it comes to block.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן might decree against the brother as a fence around the ex-husband.
steps.terutzMaskana: No such decree was made. She is permitted to the brother.
steps.whatToRemember: In this first version, רב forbids her to the ex-husband because she knows his signals. The brother stays permitted, and no decree was made against him.

steps.title: Second version: she is forbidden to the brothers too
steps.stepSummary: Some report רב יצחק בר אשיאן differently. Just as she is forbidden to the man who divorced her, she is forbidden to his brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say a different version. רב יצחק בר אשיאן said: just as she is forbidden to him, she is forbidden to the brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another version of רב יצחק בר אשיאן's statement, and it reaches the opposite result about the brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version the brother was permitted. Here the ban is stretched to cover the ex-husband's brothers too. This directly reverses the conclusion of step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say. Introduces a different version of the same statement.
Just as... so too. Compares two cases.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the versions. The first says the brother is permitted. This one says the brothers are forbidden.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
Rav Yitzchak bar Ashyan said:
Just as she is forbidden to him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the man who divorced her.

phrases.english: so she is forbidden to the brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of step 19 that reverses the ruling about the brother.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The girl is forbidden both to the man who divorced her and to his brothers.

steps.title: But she does not know the brothers' signals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second version. The worry about secret signals does not apply to the brothers, so why ban them?
steps.simpleTranslation: But she does not recognize their winks and their hints!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new version from step 22. The reason for the ban does not fit the brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole basis of the ban was her familiarity with the ex-husband's private signals. The brothers are strangers to her in that way. So forbidding them seems to have no reason behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely. Opens a challenge.

phrases.english: But she does not recognize
their winks and their hints?
phrases.notes: "Their" means the brothers'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that she is forbidden to the brothers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason for the ban (knowing his signals) is missing with the brothers.

steps.title: A decree on the brothers because of the ex-husband
steps.stepSummary: The ban on the brothers is a rabbinic decree. It protects against people allowing her to the ex-husband himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree: the brother is forbidden because of him, the ex-husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 23. The brothers are forbidden not for their own sake, but as a fence around the ex-husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version accepts exactly the decree that the first version rejected in step 21. If she married a brother, people might come to think she may marry the ex-husband too. So the רבנן banned the brothers as well.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree, a protective ban.

steps.whatToRemember: The two versions disagree about one question: did the רבנן decree against the brothers because of the ex-husband? Version one says no, version two says yes.

phrases.english: It is a decree: his brother because of him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the ruling as a protective rabbinic decree rather than a direct application of the original reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the reason of signals, there is no basis to forbid the brothers.
steps.terutzMaskana: The brothers are forbidden by decree, so that people do not permit her to the ex-husband.

steps.title: New משנה: a remarried divorcee may go to the יבם
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. If a man divorced his wife and then took her back, she is permitted to the יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a man divorces his wife and then takes her back, she is permitted to the יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins here with a new case. A man divorced his wife and remarried her, and later she comes before his brother for יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though she was divorced from this man for a while, the second marriage is what counts. So she is permitted to the יבם like any other widow. The משנה continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, our משנה. A new משנה begins.
He took her back, remarried her.
The brother of a man who died without children. He may do יבום with the widow.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who divorces his wife and takes her back
phrases.notes: The משנה means he later dies without children. That is why the יבם comes up.

phrases.english: she is permitted to the yavam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of רב's ruling ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman whose husband divorced her and then remarried her is permitted to the יבם.
